description: The filing-status input selects the imported 2026 threshold; callers do not supply a policy amount.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Inside its declared tax-year-2026 window the pre-fix pipeline left the section 199A policy amounts caller-determined - the Rev. Proc. 2025-32 threshold as a free runtime input and the section 199A(i) $1,000/$400 minimums as the statute's COLA-scaled rules keyed to a caller-supplied `minimum_deduction_cost_of_living_adjustment` - although 199A(i)(3) allows that increase only "In the case of any taxable year beginning after 2026" and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.26 fixes the 2026 thresholds.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read: resolve_provision on us/statute/26/199A returned 199A(i) in full - (i)(1)(B) "$400", (i)(2)(A) "is at least $1,000", and (i)(3) "In the case of any taxable year beginning after 2026, the $400 amount in paragraph (1)(B) and the $1,000 amount in paragraph (2)(A) shall each be increased". Two distinct halves in one commit. (a) COLA half (durable): parent 26/199A.yaml exposes `active_qbi_minimum_threshold` and `minimum_active_qbi_deduction_amount` as base + floor(base*minimum_deduction_cost_of_living_adjustment/5 + 0.5)*5 with effective_from 2026-01-01 and no effective_to, so the pre-fix 2026 pipeline would silently return non-statutory 2026 minimums for any nonzero COLA input; the fix imports `active_qbi_minimum_threshold_base`/`minimum_active_qbi_deduction_base`, adds local rule `pipeline_applicable_taxpayer_for_minimum_active_qbi_deduction` (aggregate active QBI >= 1000), drops the COLA input, and adds `versions[0].effective_to` proof atoms quoting the after-2026 clause. This half survives unchanged on main (verified in main:...pipeline.yaml lines 98-99, 419-504). (b) Threshold half (transient): the import target `us:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/qualified-business-income#qualified_business_income_threshold_amount` does not exist in the rev-proc module as of this commit - that file has only the nine per-category rules (`qualified_business_income_threshold_joint|separate|all_other`, range ends, widths); PROGRESS.md in this same commit says it was validated "In a temporary integration worktree containing cached `origin/fed-parity/revproc`". Same-day follow-up 652125375 ("fix: validate QBID threshold return category") reverts this import back to `qualified_business_income_threshold_amount_2026` plus a return-category attestation, and 7f2603e88 ("fix: import 2026 QBID threshold parameters") then imports the nine real parameters with a local filing-status selector, renamed by db9533dad. So if the corpus entry is keyed on the threshold half it captures a reverted intermediate state; keying on the COLA/effective-period half is safer. Alternative readings a reviewer may prefer: untraceable_branch (ungrounded caller-supplied policy values re-grounded on encoded sources) for the threshold half; or a mechanical/provenance reading, since no fixture expected output changed (the .test.yaml diff only rewires inputs: drops the threshold and COLA inputs, moves filing_status from the 199A namespace to the pipeline namespace) and the pre-fix module explicitly documented the threshold as a runtime input ("RuleSpec imports cannot substitute the official 2026 amount"), i.e. it never claimed to encode it. Commit body is empty; commit subject is "fix: source 2026 QBID policy values"; PROGRESS.md in the same commit states verbatim: "Replaced the QBID threshold runtime input with the PR #1009 Rev. Proc. module import and replaced the caller-supplied COLA with the unadjusted statutory $1,000/$400 bases for 2026." PR #1004 (no reviews or review comments captured) describes the head state, not this commit, and records the related review finding as "the 9th (threshold provenance) by the #1009 import at this head". The commit also reworded the module summary, source_verification rationale, and a waiver `reason`/`source_values` entry (metadata only). Note both new import proof atoms reuse hash sha256:caa63943...b816 for two different targets, which looks like a stale/duplicated hash but is outside fidelity scope.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes no effective_from, effective_to, version window or period kind anywhere: every rule keeps '2026-01-01'/'2026-12-31' before and after, and the only period-flavored edits are two newly ADDED `kind: effective_period` proof atoms (metadata/provenance), plus the window on a brand-new rule that copies the module's existing 2026 window. What actually changed in meaning is grounding: the threshold formula stops reading a free caller input and reads an imported Rev. Proc. 2025-32 value, and the 199A(i) minimum stops flowing through the statute's COLA-escalated rules (base x caller-supplied `minimum_deduction_cost_of_living_adjustment`) and reads the unadjusted $400/$1,000 bases, with the caller COLA input deleted. Since 199A(i)(3) reads "In the case of any taxable year beginning after 2026, the $400 amount in paragraph (1)(B) and the $1,000 amount in paragraph (2)(A) shall each be increased" (verified through the pinned release), the pre-fix pipeline computed a 2026 result through a provision that does not apply to 2026 and left a source-fixed threshold caller-determined — a value/formula grounded on the wrong provision or on nothing, which the fix re-grounds. That is untraceable_branch, not wrong_period_or_effective_date; the first reader's quote (a summary sentence about filing-status selection of an imported threshold) carries no period content at all.
triage.verifier_notes:
Files read: bundle JSON + diff at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/c73258bc3d/000.diff; pre/post of /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/us/policies/income_tax/qualified_business_income_deduction_pipeline.yaml; /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/us/statutes/26/199A.yaml; /Users/maxghenis/TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us/us/policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/qualified-business-income.yaml; the .test.yaml and PROGRESS.md diffs; and 26 USC 199A via resolve_provision.py (expression_date 2026-07-13).

Grounds a reviewer should weigh before accepting even "fidelity":
1. Both halves remove a boundary the module had DECLARED and documented, not a wrong value. Pre-fix summary: "accepts the applicable Revenue Procedure 2025-32 threshold as a runtime input"; pre-fix deferred_outputs reason: "RuleSpec imports cannot replace that internal parameter." The removed COLA input's own description said "Section 199A(i)(3) adjustment used only after 2026; zero for the tax-year-2026 fixtures", and every fixture supplied 0 and the documented Rev. Proc. thresholds. So no companion result changed; what changed is that a source-fixed amount can no longer be set wrong by a caller (fail-open on a policy parameter). A reviewer who treats declared caller boundaries as scope rather than defect should call this unclear/not_a_defect.
2. At this commit the import target does not exist. `us:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/qualified-business-income#qualified_business_income_threshold_amount` is listed in that module's `deferred_outputs` (its rules are only the nine per-category parameters); the pipeline summary says the import lands "through PR #1009". PR #1004's final body describes the head as importing "the nine per-category 2026 parameters ... and selects at the pipeline's declared filing-status boundary via pipeline-scoped selector rules" — i.e. this intermediate shape was superseded before merge.
3. If a reviewer wants a genuine wrong_period defect here, it is upstream and untouched: in us/statutes/26/199A.yaml, `active_qbi_minimum_threshold` and `minimum_active_qbi_deduction_amount` both carry `effective_from: '2026-01-01'` with no after-2026 gating, so they apply (i)(3) escalation from 2026 itself. This commit works around that upstream window defect by importing the `_base` parameters; it does not fix the window.
4. The commit body is bare ("fix: source 2026 QBID policy values"). The most explicit statement of intent is PROGRESS.md in the same commit (not the module, so not used as the quote): "Replaced the QBID threshold runtime input with the PR #1009 Rev. Proc. module import and replaced the caller-supplied COLA with the unadjusted statutory $1,000/$400 bases for 2026." That is sourcing/grounding language, consistent with untraceable_branch and inconsistent with a date/window correction.
5. No numeric literal changed inside this module, so amount_mismatch does not fit either; entity/scope, boolean logic and comparison strictness are untouched (the new rule's `>=` mirrors the upstream rule it replaces).
